ety.text: Proto-Germanic *tōder. Proto-West Germanic tō Proto-Indo-European *gʰedʰ-der. Proto-Germanic *gadarder. Proto-West Germanic gadura Proto-West Germanic *tōgadurader. Old English tōgædere Middle English togedere English together From Late Middle English together, from earlier togedere, togadere, from Old English tōgædere (“together”), from Proto-West Germanic *tōgadura, *tegadura, from Proto-Germanic *tō (“to”) + *gadar (“together”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰedʰ- (“to unite, keep”), equivalent to to-₂ + gather.

senses.d: At the same time, in the same place; in close association or proximity.
ex: We can't all talk together; let's take turns politely.

senses.d: Into one place; into a single thing; combined.
ex: He put all the parts together.

senses.d: In a relationship or partnership, for example a business relationship or a romantic partnership.
ex: Bob and Andy went into business together.  Jenny and Mark have been together since they went on holiday to Mexico.

senses.d: Without intermission or interruption; continuously; uninterruptedly.
ex: It has been raining four days together
Youthful, former fashion model & dancer needs to find a serious, together individual to call his own.
